slides.heading: Counters
slides.body: Counters is part of Indefinite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Counters
slides.body: A counter is a variable that changes by a regular amount each loop cycle. It is often used to count repetitions.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A counter is like counting laps while running around a track.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Every while loop needs a condition that can eventually become False, unless you intentionally stop it with break.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a counter that prints 1 to 5.
slides.hint: Add 1 to counter inside the loop.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Use a counter to print Count 1, Count 2, Count 3.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
